 Keep a close watch on these pair of Utah Jazz players in their second game of the regular season. Jared Koch | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source Apr 7, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Utah Jazz center Kyle Filipowski (22) defends against New Orleans Pelicans center Derik Queen (22) during the first half at Smoothie King Center. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In this story:
 Utah Jazz The Utah Jazz's home opener and second game of the 2026-27 regular season campaign is right around the corner–– and they'll be looking for a bounce-back performance against the New Orleans Pelicans , who have also started their new year off at an 0-1 record.
--> The Utah Jazz's home opener and second game of the 2026-27 regular season campaign is right around the corner–– and they'll be looking for a bounce-back performance against the New Orleans Pelicans , who have also started their new year off at an 0-1 record.
 In front of a buzzing home crowd in Utah, and being rested up from their prior loss against the Memphis Grizzlies , there's good reason to have a bit more optimism for what this game could end up looking like for the Jazz.
--> In front of a buzzing home crowd in Utah, and being rested up from their prior loss against the Memphis Grizzlies , there's good reason to have a bit more optimism for what this game could end up looking like for the Jazz.
 However, in the midst of the Jazz's second game of their 82-game campaign, this team could benefit from a couple of small rotation adjustments; particularly to get two players more involved than they were against Memphis to patch some of the weaknesses they proved to have back on Wednesday.
--> However, in the midst of the Jazz's second game of their 82-game campaign, this team could benefit from a couple of small rotation adjustments; particularly to get two players more involved than they were against Memphis to patch some of the weaknesses they proved to have back on Wednesday.
 Let's break down each case for the two Jazz players who deserve more minutes against the Pelicans on Friday night:
--> Let's break down each case for the two Jazz players who deserve more minutes against the Pelicans on Friday night:
 Kyle Filipowski
--> Kyle Filipowski
 Mar 28, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Utah Jazz forward Kyle Filipowski (22) against the Phoenix Suns at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In the Jazz's season opener against the Grizzlies, it wound up being a pretty limited night for big man Kyle Filipowski, who only played in nine minutes off the bench to record three points on 1-2 shooting, along with one steal.
--> In the Jazz's season opener against the Grizzlies, it wound up being a pretty limited night for big man Kyle Filipowski, who only played in nine minutes off the bench to record three points on 1-2 shooting, along with one steal.
 And the reason for Filipowski's limitations might be attributed to the ongoing ramp up from his offseason back surgery . He only played in one preseason game throughout Utah's four-game slate because he was still in the rehab process, yet was able to return to the lineup back in time for the regular season opener.
--> And the reason for Filipowski's limitations might be attributed to the ongoing ramp up from his offseason back surgery . He only played in one preseason game throughout Utah's four-game slate because he was still in the rehab process, yet was able to return to the lineup back in time for the regular season opener.
 Perhaps Filipowski isn't fully ready to sustain a full workload coming off an injury. If that's the case, then maybe the Jazz shouldn't push Filipowski beyond his limits.
--> Perhaps Filipowski isn't fully ready to sustain a full workload coming off an injury. If that's the case, then maybe the Jazz shouldn't push Filipowski beyond his limits.
 However, if at 100%, Utah should certainly hand their young big man a bigger share of the minutes in the frontcourt in an effort to offer more size, offensive versatility, and rebounding ability at the five.
--> However, if at 100%, Utah should certainly hand their young big man a bigger share of the minutes in the frontcourt in an effort to offer more size, offensive versatility, and rebounding ability at the five.
 The Jazz are slim in their big man rotation without Jusuf Nurkic, who's still stuck sidelined due to a foot injury he sustained in the preseason. It's tough to replace his presence on the front lines, but someone like Filipowski might be a bit of a band-aid on those troubles that immediately surfaced in Utah's opener in Memphis.
--> The Jazz are slim in their big man rotation without Jusuf Nurkic, who's still stuck sidelined due to a foot injury he sustained in the preseason. It's tough to replace his presence on the front lines, but someone like Filipowski might be a bit of a band-aid on those troubles that immediately surfaced in Utah's opener in Memphis.
 Last game, the Jazz were outrebounded by a whopping total of 55-38. Utah can't afford a repeat of that at home against New Orleans, and by playing someone like Filipowski, who led the team in total rebounds last season, that outcome on the boards could certainly change for the better.
--> Last game, the Jazz were outrebounded by a whopping total of 55-38. Utah can't afford a repeat of that at home against New Orleans, and by playing someone like Filipowski, who led the team in total rebounds last season, that outcome on the boards could certainly change for the better.
 Mo Bamba
--> Mo Bamba
 Oct 12, 2026; Salt Lake City, Utah, USA; Utah Jazz center Mo Bamba (44) reacts during the second half against the San Antonio Spurs at Delta Center. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Baker-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The argument for Bamba's case to get more minutes for the Jazz against the Pelicans is relatively similar to why Filipowski is due for more run: Bamba provides more size and rebounding ability for a frontcourt that's in desperate need of both aspects in the short term.
--> The argument for Bamba's case to get more minutes for the Jazz against the Pelicans is relatively similar to why Filipowski is due for more run: Bamba provides more size and rebounding ability for a frontcourt that's in desperate need of both aspects in the short term.
 Bamba might not be the stable, consistent rotational player that Filipowski has shown to be all throughout last season. However, he did showcase in preseason that he has the chance to be a quality rebounder when given the opportunity.
--> Bamba might not be the stable, consistent rotational player that Filipowski has shown to be all throughout last season. However, he did showcase in preseason that he has the chance to be a quality rebounder when given the opportunity.
 Bamba played in an average of around 12 minutes a night during each of the Jazz's four preseason games, where he was near the top of the entire roster for rebounds per game (6.8). He also ended up chipping in for 5.8 points per game on an impressive 71.4% from the field.
--> Bamba played in an average of around 12 minutes a night during each of the Jazz's four preseason games, where he was near the top of the entire roster for rebounds per game (6.8). He also ended up chipping in for 5.8 points per game on an impressive 71.4% from the field.
 And for a game in which Utah's big man rotation will be limited to just Jaxson Hayes and Kyle Filipowski, there's a real argument that Bamba shouldn't continue to be a DNP-CD like he was against the Grizzlies last game.
--> And for a game in which Utah's big man rotation will be limited to just Jaxson Hayes and Kyle Filipowski, there's a real argument that Bamba shouldn't continue to be a DNP-CD like he was against the Grizzlies last game.
 The Jazz made an emphasis earlier this offseason to go out and sign Bamba to the main roster for the premise of adding more depth to their center position.
--> The Jazz made an emphasis earlier this offseason to go out and sign Bamba to the main roster for the premise of adding more depth to their center position.
 And on Friday night, there's a perfect opening for Utah to throw Bamba into the rotation––even if only for about 10 minutes––and see just how he helps their frontcourt become a bit more well-rounded than it was in their first game of the season.
